title_en: I Disgraced Myself at the Vice City Zoo, and It’s the One Thing I’ll Never Do Again in GTA 6
summary_en: I visited the zoo in GTA 6 to commit the worst crime imaginable, and now I feel terrible.
body_en:
Regrets, I’ve had a few. But none in my over 100 hours with GTA 6 are quite like this.
It all began on a quiet afternoon in Vice City. It was a perfect day as the sun hung high in the sky, casting long shadows across the beach as vacation-goers and locals alike enjoyed the weather. An even darker, more sinister shadow would soon be cast over the city, though. A slice of paradise soon to be tarnished by the actions of one curious deviant: Me.
I took Jason for a quiet break from his life of crime to Wildland Zoo, intent on watching the flamingos have a little wade, chat with a parrot, catch a sleeping tiger looking all peaceful, or maybe sipping on a frozen mango daiquiri at its beachside bar. That was the plan, anyway.
You see, this sojourn happened right in the middle of my quest to hit GTA 6’s six-star wanted level . To do this, you really have to go out of your way to commit some pretty heinous atrocities. I’d tried mass murder. Even dabbled in a little domestic terrorism. But, alas, I was yet to max out those iconic wanted stars. So, a thought crossed my mind. A disgracefully dark one: the cages that house these animals have gaps between bars wide enough to fit a bullet through.
I didn’t act on the observation straight away, instead choosing to enjoy this pocket of peace amidst the chaos that I’d carved out for myself. But the voice in my head wouldn’t stop. “What if?” I thought to myself. What if this was the way to bring the heaviest of Leonida’s law enforcement descending upon me? I just had to try. In the name of science. In the name of ending my curiosity.
And so I prowled the pathways between enclosures, mirroring the nearby big cats who could easily have become my prey. I nervously waited for the right time to pull my revolver out of my pocket, my fingers slightly trembling in anticipation of what horrors I was about to enact. At least, I hoped it wasn’t out of excitement. I didn’t want to enjoy this. I just knew it had to happen.
The slightly rusted cages home to several Western Chimpanzees called to me, as if my dark desires acted as magnets towards their metal bars. Their inhabitants all looked happy enough. One sat on a high platform, playing with a soccer ball — besmirching the beautiful game like only a FIFA President knows how wasn’t my goal here, so I left him alone.
Below them sat a chimp cradling a piece of fruit between his feet. It looked like guava, but could so easily have been mango, just like one that produced the juice I’d been drinking just moments before. Perhaps it was a papaya, but that really is beside the point. All I knew was that it would be the final thing he tasted. Aside from lead, that is.
And so I took aim at his furry head, saying goodbye to any innocence left within me. One bang and it was done. The world stopped for a moment as I fell numb, an eerie silence filling the air where exotic birdsong and laughter once mixed. They would be replaced by shrill cries just a moment later, the surviving chimps in the cage cowering in fear, thinking they might be next. The neighbouring macaques were equally distressed. There would be no more death that day, though. In truth, it was enough for a whole lifetime, something never to be repeated.
Security wasn't best pleased. Park attendants stood in horror. Tourists fled. It was Harambe 2.0. I could already imagine the headlines:
“Local Man Shoots Ape’s Brains Out Amid Wild Scenes at Wildland Zoo”
“Chimp Blown to Bits as Tourists Run for Cover”
“Bring Back Death Penalty for Ape Killer”
Who was I to say they were wrong, either? I could hear the distant sirens approaching and, in my final act of cowardice, I didn’t even stay to face the music. I ran away. Didn’t even bother fetching my car. Just ran.
Images wouldn’t stop racing through my mind. What would those chimpanzees from the old British TV commercials for PG Tips teabags think of me now? I used to love their antics. Talking chimps dressed in human clothes? It was the height of ‘90s wit. We didn’t know how good we had it. I’d let them down. All of them.
I thought about my newfound friends in the vigilante animal rights organisation, Dodo Rising, and how once they’d hear of my crimes, they’d never text me again. They’d turn up at my court hearing, protesting outside the building, holding placards with a smiling chimp on them, chanting “Primates, not Prime-Hate” with increasing ferocity.
It was all for naught, too. This abhorrent act only triggered a one-star wanted level — back to Ocean Beach, I’d have to go to slaughter as many humans as possible. The price within me felt much heavier, though. I still hear the desperate cries for help echoing from those cages in my dreams. A curse to carry with me forevermore. Despite having mowed down several hundred people during my playthrough, it just never garnered the same reaction from me that this one animal did. I’m not quite sure what that says about me.
Regrets, I’ve had a few. But none quite like this. I did it my way. I just wish I hadn’t.
